label: Great Pacific Garbage Patch
sub: ~79,000 metric tons of plastic across 1.6M km². Primary target for The Ocean Cleanup's oceanic systems.

label: The Ocean Cleanup HQ
sub: Rotterdam, Netherlands. Global headquarters, engineering hub, and home to R&D for ocean and river cleanup technology since 2013.

label: System 001 Launch Site
sub: Alameda, California. System 001 departed from here on September 8, 2018, cheered by over 100,000 livestream viewers.

label: Interceptor 001 – Klang River
sub: Selangor, Malaysia. Deployed October 2019. Solar-powered autonomous river cleanup system in one of Southeast Asia's most plastic-polluted rivers.

label: Interceptor 002 – Cengkareng Drain
sub: Jakarta, Indonesia. Deployed November 2019. Indonesia is the world's 2nd-largest ocean plastic contributor. The Interceptor collects tonnes of plastic weekly.

label: Interceptor 003 – Can Tho River
sub: Can Tho, Vietnam. Part of the Mekong Delta river system, one of the highest-volume plastic-transport waterways in Southeast Asia.

label: Interceptor 004 – Río Ozama
sub: Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. First Interceptor in the Caribbean, deployed in partnership with the Dominican Republic government; has intercepted 300+ tonnes of waste since 2020. On Aug 16, 2026, The Ocean Cleanup and the Dominican Republic announced it will be replaced by a 400-meter barrier — the organization's largest yet — to handle seasonal water hyacinth blooms, with deployment planned for early 2027 as the opening move of the 30 Cities Program.

label: Great Barrier Reef
sub: Queensland, Australia. World's largest coral reef system (344,000 km²). Suffered its 7th mass bleaching event in 2024; 73% of surveyed area bleached. AIMS's Aug 10, 2026 annual survey found hard coral cover recovering in the Northern (35.1%) and Central (31.6%) regions as a cooler monsoon limited bleaching, though the Southern region slipped to 26.4%.

label: Mesoamerican Reef
sub: Belize/Mexico. World's second-largest barrier reef system. Active coral restoration by SECORE International and local partners; heat-tolerant corals being seeded.

label: Coral Triangle
sub: Indonesia/Philippines/Malaysia. Contains 76% of all known coral species and 37% of reef fish species. Faces threats from bleaching, fishing, and coastal development.

label: Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument
sub: Hawaii, USA. 1.5 million km² MPA — one of the world's largest. Designated 2006, expanded 2016. Protects critical habitat for Hawaiian monk seals, sea turtles, and seabirds.

label: Chagos Archipelago / BIOT MPA
sub: British Indian Ocean Territory. 640,000 km² no-take MPA designated 2010. Contains some of the world's most pristine coral reefs; sovereignty contested between UK and Mauritius.

label: Ross Sea MPA
sub: Antarctica. World's largest MPA at 1.55 million km², established by CCAMLR in 2016. Protects one of Earth's last near-pristine ocean ecosystems.

label: North Atlantic Garbage Patch
sub: Sargasso Sea accumulation zone. High concentration of microplastics and macroplastics driven by North Atlantic subtropical gyre circulation. Threatens unique Sargassum seaweed ecosystem.

label: South Pacific Garbage Patch
sub: South Pacific subtropical gyre. Estimated 70,000+ metric tons of plastic floating in this accumulation zone; less studied than GPGP but equally concerning.

label: Mediterranean Sea Plastic Hotspot
sub: Semi-enclosed sea with among the world's highest plastic concentrations: ~1,800 plastic items per km². Receives heavy input from European and North African rivers.

label: Bay of Bengal Plastic Hotspot
sub: Receives massive plastic inputs from the Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna river system (India, Bangladesh). Among the world's highest plastic-loading coastal regions.

label: South Georgia & South Sandwich Islands
sub: UK Overseas Territory with 1 million km² MPA. Critical humpback and blue whale feeding ground. Humpback population recovering strongly since end of industrial whaling.

label: Gulf of St. Lawrence – Right Whale Habitat
sub: Canada. Critical foraging ground for critically endangered North Atlantic Right Whales (~356 individuals). Ship speed restrictions and seasonal fishing closures enforced since 2017.

label: Bering Sea – North Pacific Right Whale
sub: Alaska, USA. Critical habitat for the critically endangered North Pacific Right Whale — fewer than 500 individuals estimated. Faces entanglement and ship strike risks.

label: Ghana Marine Protected Area
sub: Gulf of Guinea, West Africa. Ghana's first MPA, designated April 14, 2026, after 15+ years of advocacy. Co-managed with local fishing communities to support fisheries recovery and coastal biodiversity.

label: Interceptor – Meycauayan River
sub: Bulacan, Philippines. First Ocean Cleanup Interceptor in the Philippines, deployed May 2026. Part of the 30 Cities Program; projected to intercept 370–540 tonnes of plastic annually before it reaches Manila Bay.

label: Caribbean Reef Collapse Zone
sub: Caribbean Basin. A May 2026 peer-reviewed study found 70% of Caribbean coral reefs shifted from net growth to net erosion due to the 2023-24 marine heatwave — years ahead of modeled timelines. Heat stress was 2-3x any prior record.

label: Kenya Northern Coast – Coral Restoration
sub: Kenya's northern coastline. Canon and Oceans Alive Foundation launched a coral reef restoration initiative in May 2026, scaling up coral nursery propagation and reef rehabilitation with underwater imaging monitoring to track fish populations and bleaching events.

label: Interceptor – Los Angeles River
sub: Los Angeles, California, USA. May 2026 expansion: Kia and The Ocean Cleanup announced Interceptor deployment on the LA River as part of the 30 Cities Program, building on Interceptor 007 in Ballona Creek. The broader LA river system emits 380–570 tonnes of plastic annually into the Pacific Ocean, timed ahead of LA28 Olympics.

label: Interceptor – San Gabriel River
sub: Long Beach, California, USA. Announced May 2026 as part of The Ocean Cleanup's 30 Cities Program expansion in Greater Los Angeles. The San Gabriel River drains heavily urbanized inland valleys, transporting significant quantities of plastic debris toward San Pedro Bay and the Pacific Ocean.

label: Interceptor – Trombay Creek
sub: Mumbai, India. The Ocean Cleanup deployed Interceptor barriers in Trombay Creek in May 2026, in partnership with BMC and MPCB. One of two Mumbai pilot sites; once operational during monsoon season, each system recovers 30–46 tonnes of plastic per year. Mumbai's waterways discharge an estimated 5 million kg of plastic annually into the Arabian Sea.

label: Interceptor – Malad Creek
sub: Mumbai, India (northwestern suburbs). Second Mumbai pilot site deployed May 2026 as part of The Ocean Cleanup's 30 Cities Program and India entry. Malad Creek drains densely populated northwest Mumbai suburbs before meeting the Arabian Sea. Operations led by social enterprise Plastic Fischer, with community support from United Way Mumbai.

label: Florida Reef Tract – Early Bleaching Zone
sub: South Florida, USA. By May 28, 2026, approximately 25% of corals near PortMiami showed early bleaching signs — months ahead of the typical July–October bleaching season. By July 12, 2026, USGS scientists confirmed visible bleaching of starlet and lobed star coral at Newfound Harbor in the Lower Florida Keys, as El Niño conditions strengthened and NOAA Coral Reef Watch raised Alert Level 1 across most of coastal Florida. Scientists from the University of Miami's Rescue a Reef program are transplanting heat-tolerant 'super corals' ahead of another potentially record-breaking hot summer. Florida has lost over 90% of its coral cover since the 1970s.

label: Pacific Gray Whale Stranding Zone
sub: Washington State, USA. 22+ gray whale carcasses washed ashore along Washington's Pacific coast in spring 2026, part of a mortality event that pushed 2026 coastwide strandings to 145 from Mexico to Alaska, prompting researchers and PEER to declare a 'catastrophic mortality event.' However, NOAA's July 15, 2026 migration survey estimated the live population at ~17,750 (95% CI: 15,930–20,530) — a rebound from 2024/25's ~11,700–14,200 that complicates the collapse narrative, even as calf production remains near record lows. Scientists link continued die-offs to Arctic sea ice loss disrupting the benthic amphipod food chain, forcing whales onto far less nutritious warm-water jellyfish.

label: Mia-yaltwa Ha'lidzogm hoon — BC Central Coast MPA
sub: British Columbia, Canada. May 22, 2026: Six First Nations (Wuikinuxv, Nuxalk, Kitasoo Xai'xais, Heiltsuk, Gitxaała, Gitga'at) signed a landmark agreement with Canada and BC establishing the first dual National Marine Conservation Area Reserve + Indigenous Protected and Conserved Area with the same footprint. Name means 'Realm of the Salmon, Home of the Salmon.' Protects Pacific salmon, orca, and humpback whale habitat on BC's Central Coast.

label: Rice's Whale — Gulf of Mexico Critical Habitat
sub: Northern Gulf of Mexico. The Rice's whale (Balaenoptera ricei) — also known as the Gulf of Mexico whale — is one of the world's most endangered large whales with an estimated population of fewer than 100 individuals, its entire range confined to the northern Gulf of Mexico. On June 3, 2026, Oceana and Earthjustice filed suit against the Trump administration for invoking the ESA 'God Squad' exemption to strip federal endangered species protections from the Rice's whale and 19 other Gulf species to facilitate offshore oil and gas drilling expansion.
